'''Robert Eric Ricklefs''' (June 6, 1943 – June 7, 2026) was an American ornithologist and ecologist. He was the Curators' Professor of Biology at the [[University of Missouri, St. Louis]] from 1996 until August 2019.

==Early life and education==
Born on June 6, 1943, he grew up near [[Monterey, California]], where his interest in biology was fostered by a teacher.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-28 |title=Noted ecologist and ornithologist Bob Ricklefs aims to remain involved at UMSL even after retirement |url=https://blogs.umsl.edu/news/2019/08/28/ricklefs-retirement/ |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=UMSL Daily}}</ref> He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] from Stanford University in 1963 and a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania in 1967. His doctoral advisor was originally [[Robert H. MacArthur]] (prior to his move to Princeton University), but he finished his dissertation under W. John Smith.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Gillespie |first=Rosemary G. |date=2011 |title=Interview with Robert E. Ricklefs, recipient of the 2011 Alfred Russel Wallace award |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/1zb8z229 |journal=Frontiers of Biogeography |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |doi=10.21425/F5FBG12391|s2cid=83880583 |doi-access=free }}</ref> During his PhD, he studied avian growth and development, which he continued for much of his career. He completed a year as a [[Postdoctoral research|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute]] in Panama before taking up a faculty position at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He was the 1982 recipient of the [[American Ornithologists' Union]]'s William Brewster Memorial Award, the union's most prestigious award given annually for an exceptional body of work on birds of the Western Hemisphere.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |title=Brewster Award, 1982: Robert E. Ricklefs |url=https://academic.oup.com/auk/article/100/1/268/5187296 |access-date=2022-09-28 |journal=The Auk | year=1983 | volume=100 | page=268 |doi=10.1093/auk/100.1.268|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2003, he received the [[Pacific Seabird Group]]'s Lifetime Achievement Award for his work on growth and development in seabirds.<ref name=":3">[http://www.pacificseabirdgroup.org/publications/PacificSeabirds/VOL_30_1_pgs_1-41.PDF Pacific Seabirds Vol. 30]</ref> He was awarded the 2003 [[Margaret Morse Nice Medal]] by the [[Wilson Ornithological Society]].<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url= http://www.wilsonsociety.org/awards/nicemedal.html|archive-url= https://archive.today/20121209083324/http://www.wilsonsociety.org/awards/nicemedal.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= 2012-12-09|title= Margaret Morse Nice Medal|access-date= 2012-04-09|publisher= Wilson Ornithological Society|date= 2010-05-29}}</ref>  He was the 2006 recipient of the [[Cooper Ornithological Society]]’s [[Loye and Alden Miller Research Award]], which is given in recognition of lifetime achievement in [[ornithology|ornithological research]].<ref name=":5">[http://www.cooper.org/COS/COS_award_miller.html COS: Miller Awards] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070814155154/http://www.cooper.org/COS/COS_award_miller.html |date=2007-08-14 }}</ref>

==Research==
During his career,<ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|0Gx2tTMAAAAJ}}</ref> he has made major contributions to the [[island biogeography]], including testing [[E. O. Wilson]]'s [[Taxon cycle|Taxon Cycle Concept]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ricklefs | first1 = Robert. E. | last2 = Cox | first2 = George W. | year = 1972 | title = Taxon Cycles in the West Indian Avifauna | journal = The American Naturalist | volume = 106 | issue = 948 | pages = 195–219 | jstor = 2459928 | doi=10.1086/282762| bibcode = 1972ANat..106..195R | s2cid = 84412686 }}</ref> His most-cited scientific paper examined ecological communities.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Ricklefs | first1 = R. E. | author-link = Robert Ricklefs| title = Community Diversity: Relative Roles of Local and Regional Processes | doi = 10.1126/science.235.4785.167 | journal = Science | volume = 235 | issue = 4785 | pages = 167–171 | year = 1987 | pmid =  17778629| bibcode = 1987Sci...235..167R | s2cid = 2792273 }}</ref> Recent work has sought to rescale the concept of an [[ecological community]].<ref>{{Cite journal 
| last1 = Ricklefs | first1 = R. E. 
| author-link = Robert Ricklefs
| title = Disintegration of the Ecological Community 
| doi = 10.1086/593002 
| journal = The American Naturalist 
| volume = 172 
| issue = 6 
| pages = 741–750 
| year = 2008 
| pmid = 18954264 
| bibcode = 2008ANat..172..741R 
| s2cid = 17464820 
}}</ref> He has made major contributions to life-history theory of birds, avian growth and development,<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last=Ricklefs |first=Robert E. |date=November 1967 |title=A Graphical Method of Fitting Equations to Growth Curves |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.2307/1934545 |journal=Ecology |language=en |volume=48 |issue=6 |pages=978–983 |doi=10.2307/1934545|jstor=1934545 |bibcode=1967Ecol...48..978R |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ricklefs |first=Robert E. |title=Patterns of Growth in Birds |date=2008-04-03 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1474-919X.1968.tb00058.x |journal=Ibis |language=en |volume=110 |issue=4 |pages=419–451 |doi=10.1111/j.1474-919X.1968.tb00058.x|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Weight Recession in Nestling Birds |journal=The Auk |doi=10.2307/4083621| jstor=4083621 | last1=Ricklefs | first1=Robert E. | year=1968 | volume=85 | issue=1 | pages=30–35 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ricklefs |first=Robert E. |title=Growth Rates of Birds in the Humid New World Tropics |date=2008-04-03 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1474-919X.1976.tb03065.x |journal=Ibis |language=en |volume=118 |issue=2 |pages=179–207 |doi=10.1111/j.1474-919X.1976.tb03065.x|url-access=subscription }}</ref> tropical ecology, and avian disease research. His original method for avian growth rate estimation<ref name=":6" /> continues to be used today though modifications have been proposed. His textbook ''Ecology,'' first published in 1973, continues to be updated and used in university courses.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Ricklefs, Robert E. |author2=Miller, Gary L. |title=Ecology |publisher=Freeman |location=San Francisco |year=2000 |isbn=0-7167-2829-X }}</ref> He has also published ''The Economy of Nature''<ref>{{cite book|title=Amazon.com: The Economy of Nature (9780716786979): Robert E. Ricklefs: Books|isbn = 978-0716786979|last1 = Ricklefs|first1 = Robert E.|date = 2008-12-11| publisher=Macmillan }}</ref>'', Avian Growth and Development: Evolution Within the Altricial-precocial Spectrum''<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Starck |first1=J. Matthias |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A0HB7Mq4lOYC&dq=avian+growth+rates+ricklefs&pg=PR15 |title=Avian Growth and Development: Evolution Within the Altricial-precocial Spectrum |last2=Ricklefs |first2=Robert E. |date=1998 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-510608-4 |language=en}}</ref> and ''Aging, A Natural History.''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ricklefs |first=Robert E. |title=Aging : a natural history |date=1995 |publisher=Scientific American Library |others=Caleb Finch |isbn=0-7167-5056-2 |location=New York |oclc=31969925}}</ref>

==Career==
*Assistant Professor, Department of Biology, [[University of Pennsylvania]], 1968–1972
*Associate Professor, Department of Biology, University of Pennsylvania, 1972–1978
*Professor, Department of Biology, University of Pennsylvania, 1978–1995
*Curators’ Professor, Department of Biology, [[University of Missouri-St. Louis]], 1995–2019<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umsl.edu/~ricklefsr/|title=Robert E|access-date=2009-06-23|archive-date=2015-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117161320/http://www.umsl.edu/~ricklefsr/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Ricklefs was married to the botanist [[Susanne Renner]].<ref name=":0" /> He died on June 7, 2026, at the age of 83.<ref>[https://news.mongabay.com/2026/06/robert-ricklefs-ecologist-who-helped-generations-understand-nature-has-died-at-83/ Robert Ricklefs, ecologist who helped generations understand nature, has died at 83]</ref>
